dedupe_keys.name: green infrastructure features and local business recovery after tropical storm imelda beaumont texas

description: This study tests whether the size, shape, connectivity and amenities of green infrastructure explain how fast local businesses recovered after Tropical Storm Imelda in Beaumont, Texas. Researchers at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and Texas A&M University published it in Urban Forestry & Urban Greening in February 2026. Coverage is one Gulf Coast city. They compare SafeGraph foot traffic to businesses before, during and after the storm with landscape indices from FRAGSTATS and hand-catalogued park features, using regression that controls for income, race and poverty. Businesses within a half mile of parks recovered better, larger and more complex-shaped parks helped most, and playgrounds were negatively associated. Format and access: the abstract and accepted manuscript on OSTI, with the publisher page blocked from the cloud; the mobility data are commercial and not released. Licence: publisher copyright and OSTI terms, not read; free to read. Caveats: correlation in one city and one event, with proprietary data. It supports resilience and hazard exposure studies of green infrastructure and recovery. A related catalogue record is ParkServe, which maps the parks that studies like this classify.
